title: Lavorano per Guess, Calvin Klein, e Tommy Hilfiger, ma guadagnano meno di 1 dollaro al giorno
description: Il settore tessile in Etiopia – il secondo paese più popoloso dell’Africa con 105 milioni di abitanti - cresce a ritmi significativi. Il governo prevede che le esportazioni del comparto, che attualmente valgono 145 milioni di dollari l'anno, salgano a circa 30 miliardi. Un obiettivo tuttavia che appare irrealistico, se non altro perché bassi salari hanno portato a una scarsa produttività, a ripetuti scioperi e a un esasperato turn over (le fabbriche sostituiscono in media tutti i loro dipendenti ogni dodici mesi). Secondo un rapporto della New York University, i lavoratori etiopi con 26 dollari al mese sono tra i meno retribuiti al mondo. E, paradossalmente, sono dipendenti di marchi globali come Guess, H&M, Calvin Klein, Gap, Tommy Hilfiger, e JC Penney che nel paese africano hanno delocalizzato i loro stabilimenti. L'Etiopia, che mira a diventare il principale centro manifatturiero del continente, ha sedotto gli investitori facendo passare il messaggio che sarebbe stato sufficiente riconoscere ai lavoratori meno di un terzo dei salari offerti in Bangladesh. E si consideri che per lo stesso lavoro i kenyoti sono pagati 207 dollari al mese e i cinesi 326.

description: Zakup gry erotycznej to krok w kierunku pozytywnej zmiany sypialnianego repertuaru. Wiele nietuzinkowych zestawów gier dla par znajduje się na stronie swiat-doznan.pl. Możliwość zapoznania się z różnymi formami i scenariuszami pozwala na dobór idealnego rozwiązania, które z pewnością rozpali atmosferę w łóżku.Zanim dwie osoby w pełni odkryją swoje potrzeby seksualne, zwykle mija dużo czasu. Z kolei nieznajomość wzajemnych pragnień może determinować mniejszą satysfakcję z erotycznych doznań. Implementacja gier erotycznych to rozwiązanie dla osób, które chcą wprowadzić ciekawy, nietuzinkowy element rozrywki do swojej łóżkowej rutyny. To właśnie te aspekty warunkują cenę poszczególnych produktów. W sklepie swiat-doznan.pl dostępne są nietuzinkowe, różnorodne zestawy, które pozwalają na odkrywcze aktywności w sferze intymnej. Implementacja gry erotycznej w swoim łóżkowym rytuale to doskonały sposób na rozpoczęcie szalonej przygody z seksem analnym czy poznanie praktyki BDSM w zupełnie inny sposób.jesteśmy bardzo zadowoleni z zestawu, który zakupiliśmy z partnerką w sklepie swiat-doznan.pl. jest to doskonały pomysł na urozmaicenie sfery seksualnej i znalezienie ciekawych pomysłów na grę wstępną. duży plus za to, że produkt dotarł do nas dyskretnie zapakowany. polecankoBartoszPolecam każdej parze, która chce, wprowadzić element pikanterii do swojego intymnego rytuału. Często dodajemy do scenariusza coś od siebie, często improwizujemy. Armut, Nahrungsmittelknappheit, häufige Überschwemmungen. Viele Menschen können nicht lesen oder schreiben, sind nicht in die moderne Ökonomie eingebunden und haben nur unzureichenden Zugang zu medizinischer Versorgung. In Äthiopien sterben heute noch immer 353 Frauen auf 100.000 Lebendgeburten. title: SCS Project Health Program Supply Chain Advisor for HIV/AIDS and TB
description: Main Purpose Of Job The Health Program Supply Chain advisor for HIV/AIDS and TB, embedded within the Ministry of Health’s Pharmaceutical and Medical Devices Lead Executive Office (PMD LEO), provides technical assistance in demand planning, resource mobilization, procurement, stock status and pipeline monitoring, and overall supply chain management of HIV/AIDS and TB program commodities. The role is designed to strengthen MOH PMD-LEO systems and is delivered under the leadership and direction of the PMD-LEO, with the explicit objective of progressively and fully transitioning responsibilities, knowledge, and support to the MOH PMD‑LEO. The Advisor works closely with MOH HIV and TB Health programs and Finance Chief Executive Office of MOH, and Ethiopian Pharmaceutical Supply Service (EPSS), to strengthen an efficient, responsive, and sustainable supply chain system for HIV/AIDS and TB products. The role focuses on improving supply chain performance through process optimization to minimize wastage, reduce costs, and enhance operational efficiency. The Advisor ensures effective inventory management, storage, distribution, and quality assurance of HIV/AIDS and TB commodities, strengthening program specific and supply chain coordination platforms, and supporting public and private sector counterparts in strengthening supply chain operations. By promoting data driven decision- making and alignment with national health program priorities, the Advisor contributes to a sustainable and resilient health supply chain system, ultimately improving access to lifesaving HIV/AIDS and TB commodities. In addition, the advisor plays a key role in capacity building efforts through technical mentorship, coaching, knowledge and skill transfer to MoH and EPSS teams to enhance long-term supply chain management capacity. Specific Responsibilities Under supervision of the Supply Chain Lead of SCS and the Supply Chain Desk Head of PMD LEO/MOH, and in close collaboration with technical teams in SCS Project and PMD LEO, the Health Program Supply Chain Advisor for HIV/AIDS and TB will carry out the following responsibilities: Provide strategic level support in developing pharmaceutical supply chain strategies, projects, and action plans while advising MoH and EPSS leadership on initiatives to enhance HIV/AIDS and TB supply chain efficiency and effectiveness. Collaborate with MoH key functions, EPSS, USG SC Project HIV and TB Supply Chain Manager as well as Forecasting and Supply Plan Manager, and other partners to strengthen the HIV/AIDS and TB commodities supply chain, ensuring accurate quantification, timely procurement, and continuous availability of required commodities across all levels of the supply chain system. Provide expert guidance to SCS management and staff on HIV/AIDS and TB-related health policies, strategies, interventions, and innovations. Work with public and private sector partners to implement HIV/AIDS and TB supply chain activities across the country, ensuring alignment with national health program strategies. Collaborate with the SCS team, MOH, EPSS, and other key stakeholders to design and implement supply chain strengthening strategies, tools, and approaches to improve HIV and TB commodity availability while conducting and supporting supply management assessments to evaluate and enhance supply chain operations. Provide technical assistance to MoH, and RHBs in translating national policies into regional and woreda-level implementation guidelines. Compile, evaluate, and maintain an evidence-based HIV/AIDS and TB-related supply chain challenges and best practices to inform advocacy, policy dialogue, and planning efforts with the Ministry of Health (MOH), Regional Health Bureaus (RHBs), Woreda health Office teams, Health facilities and implementing partners. Collaborate with SCS team, MOH, EPSS, and other key stakeholders to design and implement supply chain strengthening strategies, tools, and approaches to improve HIV/AIDS and TB commodities availability. Under the guidance of the PMD‑LEO Desk Head, serve as a liaison between the MOH, DOS, and SCS to enhance coordination and collaboration and to advance MOH supply chain priorities. Support PMDLEO in advancing overall supply chain maturity through strategic engagement at the MOH level. Strengthen coordination and alignment among MOH, EPSS, EPHI, and EFDA by serving as an effective liaison across these and other relevant stakeholders. Support forecasting and supply planning for HIV/AIDS and TB commodities, including new pediatric formulations, ensuring an uninterrupted supply of HIV/AIDS and TB program products. title: Senior Non-Key Expert – IT Audit (SNKE – Audit 9)
description: For Project: Service Contract for Technical Facility Unit (TFU) for the EU Support to Public Finance Management Reforms in Ethiopia (EUSPRE) The European Union is supporting the Government of Ethiopia through the EUSPRE public financial management (PFM) project. The EUSPRE Technical Facility Unit (TFU) provides oversight of the EUSPRE programme and specifically support and capacity building support to the Federal government’s PFM Reforms program. The Overall Objective of the EUSPRE programme is enhanced transparency and efficiency of public financial management for better service delivery and inclusive development . DAI is looking for a Senior Non-Key Expert – IT Audit (SNKE – Audit 9) to Support the Office of the Federal Auditor General (OFAG) by updating the current IT Audit Manual and Working Papers and delivering related Dissemination Workshop and Classroom Training. Scope of work The scope of work for this assignment includes the following activities/ tasks to be undertaken by the NKE, in conjunction with the OFAG designated working group led by the Director of ITAU, which are further detailed in the two sub-sections below: 1. Carry out consultations with the KE3 (TFU) and the OFAG designated working group led by Director of ITAU, and assessment of the scope of work. Prepare an Inception Report with a detailed workplan to carry out the entire assignment and deliver the outputs. 2. Review already prepared/approved Gap Analysis related to areas of manual requiring update in conjunction with KE3 (TFU) and the OFAG designated working group led by Director of ITAU. 3. Support updating of the OFAG IT Audit Manual (Version 2018) and respective Working Papers, as agreed during the inception meetings, and in line with the approved changes set within Gap Analysis, taking in consideration necessary customisation to the Ethiopian context. 4. Develop dissemination workshop materials for the updated version of IT Audit Manual and WPs, facilitate and deliver a one-day Dissemination Workshop for the Senior Management (total 40 attendees). The workshop will be a ‘kick-start’ to establish arrangements for adoption and rollout for the updated version of the OFAG IT Audit Manual (Version 2026) and respective Working Papers. 5. Develop two training modules (materials) for Classroom Trainings on the updated OFAG IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026) and new IT Audit practices practical for the ITAU Director and Auditors, FADs and P&ED Directors and Managers, AQAD and T&ED teams members (total 40 participants). 6. Facilitate and deliver training over two one-week training sessions (five days each, total ten days). First week (Module 1) is going to be delivered to 30 participants comprised of staff from ITAU and selected staff from: FADs, P&ED, AQAD and T&ED; while second week (Module 2) is going to be delivered to 10 participants referring to staff from ITAU (total 40 participants). Classroom Trainings will comprise of two training modules (materials) covering following: I. Module 1 will cover a detailed presentation of updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026): § An Introduction to updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual & WPs (Version 2026) covering: a. In-depth description and elaboration of the IT Audit Manual content: Introduction, Establishing IT Audit Function, IT Audit Standards, Frameworks and Audit Work, Planning Process, Conducting the Audit, Reporting, Follow-up, Communication, Quality Control. b. In-depth description and elaboration of the WPs content. II. Module 2 will cover practical exercises relating to the application of updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026) using IT Audit Case Study. The case study should cover all of the following topics, as agreed with OFAG Management: § An introduction to new working practices using IT Audit Case Study in form of classroom exercise as part of practical application of updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026) in the following areas: Audit of IT Governance and Segregation of Duties; Audit of Network and Systems (Hardware & Software); Audit of Active Directory and other User Management Systems; Audit of IT Security and Cybersecurity Areas; Audit of Data Centres and it’s Environment; Audit of ERP Applications and Databases; Audit of Backup Solutions and Disaster Recovery; Audit of AI and Emerging Technologies (Cloud Computing, IoT, Big Data, etc.); Audit of IT Projects and Systems under Development. 7. Prepare combined end-of-assignment report reflecting on the work delivered for updating of the OFAG IT Audit Manual (Version 2026) and respective Working Papers as well as for delivery of Dissemination Workshop and delivery of Classroom Trainings. Output(s) Deliver Inception Report with a detailed Gantt chart workplan to carry out the assignment and deliver the outputs. title: Digital Identity Lead - Frontier Technologies Foundations
description: The Digital Identity Lead is a high-visibility, dual-engine role sitting at the intersection of technical architecture and commercial origination. The role's anchor specialism is Digital Identity (DID): you will bring deep, hands-on experience of building or implementing national-scale digital identity architectures, and you will ultimately own FT's DID service line. Because identity is a load-bearing foundation beneath the rest of FT's foundations stack — every national data ecosystem depends on a trusted unique identifier, and every identity system depends on a cryptographic trust and security layer — this role is deliberately broader than a pure DID mandate. You will carry contributory technical responsibility into Data at Societal Scale (national data exchange, interoperability, data governance) and Cybersecurity (PKI, cryptographic trust frameworks, Zero Trust design), acting as FT's connective thread across these three foundations. You will not be expected to lead these adjacent domains, but to ensure DID engagements are architected coherently with them, and to lend specialist input when FT's Data and Cyber leads need identity-layer expertise. You will also act as a core business builder for the practice, using your global network within the World Bank, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and the broader DPI ecosystem to originate new projects, secure funding, and scale Genesis's pipeline across all three foundations. 1 | Key Responsibilities 1.1 Business Origination & Strategic Networks (35%) Pipeline Generation: Leverage existing, high-level relationships within the World Bank, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF), Co-Develop, and key regional development banks to position Genesis as the premier global choice for DPI implementation — opening doors for Data at Societal Scale and Cybersecurity mandates as a natural extension of DID relationships Deal Structuring & Capture: Proactively identify, shape, and capture business opportunities across the DID and foundational ID ecosystem; lead high-value proposal development and pitches for donor-funded tenders, and contribute technical input to Data and Cybersecurity pursuits where identity is a component Ecosystem Integration: Act as a primary interface between Genesis and the global identity, data, and digital government communities, aligning firm capabilities with emerging donor strategies, funding cycles, and country-level roadmaps 1.2 Digital Identity — Technical Leadership & Implementation (35%) National-Scale Delivery: Serve as the chief subject-matter expert on the architectural design, governance, and roll-out strategies of foundational or functional national digital ID systems Framework Champion: Embed international standards and best practice — specifically World Bank ID4D principles, ID4Africa frameworks, and open-source stacks such as MOSIP — into localised government roadmaps Next-Gen Identity Architecture: Advise clients on the transition toward Decentralised Identity (DID) ecosystems, Verifiable Credentials (VCs), and self-sovereign identity (SSI) frameworks Cross-Functional Integration: Ensure identity frameworks interoperate seamlessly with the other DPI pillars — payments, data exchange, and (in time) national cybersecurity architecture 1.3 Contributory Technical Leadership: Data & Cybersecurity Foundations (20%) Data at Societal Scale: Advise on how unique identifiers and civil registries underpin national data exchange and interoperability architecture; contribute an identity lens to national data strategy and data governance engagements led by FT's Data practice Cybersecurity: Bring your natural DID-adjacent expertise in cryptographic trust frameworks, PKI, and public/private key infrastructure to inform Zero Trust architecture, authentication and authorisation design, and identity-linked security posture assessments — supporting the build-out of FT's cybersecurity service line ahead of its 2027 launch Coherence Across Foundations: Act as the technical bridge ensuring DID, Data, and Cybersecurity workstreams are designed as one interoperable stack rather than three siloed engagements, in line with FT's GOAT framework (Governance, Operations, Adoption, Technology) 1.4 Practice Building & Thought Leadership (10%) Mentorship: Guide and upskill a growing team of consultants and analysts across FT's foundations pillar, fostering a culture of technical excellence beyond DID alone Global Presence: Represent Genesis at premier international forums — ID4Africa, World Bank Digital Government and Spring Meetings, and DID/data/cyber developer convenings — publishing high-impact insights and whitepapers that span the foundations stack How This Role Differs From a Pure DID Mandate Anchor specialism: Digital Identity — full ownership, national-scale delivery track record required Contributory remit: Data at Societal Scale and Cybersecurity — working fluency and cross-practice coordination, not delivery ownership Why broadened: Identity is the found

Its protection interventions in Ethiopia follow a six-pillar intervention that includes direct assistance to migrants, displaced persons and affected communities, thematic guidance, capacity development, advocacy, and research. The Protection Unit (PXU) works closely with the government of Ethiopia and various stakeholders in emergency, displacement, and migration settings to reduce protection risks and address the needs of vulnerable individuals and communities. IOM is guided by rights-based approaches across its migration programming, demonstrating commitment to the safeguarding of vulnerable groups. Request for Proposal Prequalification of Printing, Branding and Production Service Providers Ethiopia Framework Agreement (2026 – 2028) July 2026 Procurement Summary Item Description Client Girl Effect Ethiopia Assignment Prequalification of Printing, Branding & Production Service Providers Procurement Method Open Competitive Procurement Contract Type Framework Agreement Framework Period September 2026 – August 2028 Number of Suppliers Multiple suppliers may be appointed Location Ethiopia Currency Ethiopian Birr (ETB) Who We Are Girl Effect is an international non-profit organisation that creates media, technology and behaviour change programmes that empower adolescent girls and young people to improve their health, education and economic opportunities. In Ethiopia, Girl Effect delivers programmes through the Yegna youth brand, reaching millions of young people through media, digital platforms, community engagement and research. These programmes require a wide range of professionally produced printing, branding and promotional materials to support programme implementation across Ethiopia Objective Girl Effect Ethiopia seeks to establish a roster of qualified printing, branding and production service providers for a two-year Framework Agreement. Suppliers appointed to the framework may be invited to participate in: Restricted Requests for Quotations (RFQs) Mini-competitions Direct call-off assignments depending on the nature, value and complexity of future requirements. Appointment to the framework does not guarantee any minimum volume of work. Framework Period The framework agreement shall remain valid for: September 2026 –August 2028 Girl Effect reserves the right to extend the framework for an additional period, subject to satisfactory performance. What You’ll Do The selected suppliers shall be capable of providing one or more of the following services: A. Programme and Educational Materials Student Manuals /Facilitator Guides – Booklets - 60 pages Size: A5 Portrait (unless otherwise specified) Printing: Full colour (CMYK), double-sided Inside Pages: 150 GSM white bond paper, glossy Cover: 300 gsm art card with matte or gloss lamination Binding: Saddle stitched or perfect bound depending on page count Finish: Trimmed and neatly finished Discussion Guides – Flip Charts - 20 pages Size: A3 Landscape (297 × 420 mm) Printing: Full colour, double-sided Paper: 250 gsm art card, glossy Mounting: White laminated rigid board backing Type: Self-standing flip chart Finish: Durable and suitable for repeated use during training sessions Conversation Card - Flash Cards Size: A5 or A6 (as specified) Printing: Full colour, double-sided Material: 300 gsm art card Finish: Matte or gloss lamination with rounded corners where required Fact Sheets - Brochure Size: A4 or A3 folded Printing: Full colour, double-sided Paper: 170 gsm art paper Finish: Folded and neatly trimmed B. Information, Education and Communication Materials Posters Sizes: A3, A2, A1 or custom sizes Printing: Full colour, single or double-sided Paper: 200 gsm art paper Finish: Matte or gloss finish as required Flyers Size: A5 or DL Printing: Full colour, double-sided Paper: 150 gsm art paper Finish: Trimmed and bundled Leaflets Size: A4 folded to DL or A5 Printing: Full colour Paper: 150–170 gsm art paper Finish: Bi-fold or tri-fold as required Brochures Size: A4 folded (Bi-fold or Tri-fold) Printing: Full colour Paper: 170 gsm art paper Finish: Professionally folded Calendars Type: Wall or Desk Calendar Printing: Full colour Cover: 300 gsm art card Inside Pages: 170–200 gsm art paper Binding: Wire binding with hanging hook where applicable Stickers Material: Vinyl or self-adhesive paper Printing: Full colour Finish: Gloss laminated Cutting: Die-cut or kiss-cut depending on design C. Event and Activation Materials Roll-up Banners Size: 85 × 200 cm Material: Premium anti-curl banner material Printing: Full colour Includes: Aluminium stand and carrying bag Backdrops Material: 440 gsm PVC Flex or fabric Printing: Full colour Finish: Hemmed edges with eyelets Stage Branding Material: PVC Flex, fabric or foam board depending on requirement Printing: Full colour Installation: Where requested Directional Signage Material: Foam board, PVC board or Sunboard Printing: Full colour Finish: Mounted where applicable Event Badges Material: PVC card or laminated art card Printing: Full colour Includes: Lanyard where required Certificates Size: A4 Printing: Full colour Paper: 300 gsm ivory or art card Finish: Matte or gloss finish D. Branding and Promotional Materials Branded Notebooks Size: A5 or A4 Cover: 300 gsm laminated art card or hard cover Inside Pages: 80 gsm ruled or plain paper Binding: Spiral or perfect bound Branded Folders Size: A4 Material: 350 gsm art card Finish: Matte or gloss lamination Features: Business card slot and document pocket Branded Pens Plastic or metal body Single or multi-colour branding Screen printing or UV printing Branded Tote Bags Material: Heavy-duty canvas or cotton Printing: Screen printing, heat transfer or DTF printing Colour: As specified T-Shirts Material: 100% cotton (180–200 gsm) Printing: Screen printing, DTF or embroidery Sizes: Small to XXL Polo Shirts Material: Cotton pique (220 gsm) Branding: Embroidery or high-quality printing Sizes: Small to XXL Caps Material: Cotton twill Branding: Embroidery or screen printing Adjustable fastening Lanyards Material: Polyester Printing: Full-colour sublimation Includes: Metal hook and safety buckle where required Water Bottles Material: Aluminium or stainless steel Branding: UV print, screen print or laser engraving Mugs Material: Ceramic Branding: Sublimation printing Capacity: Approximately 330 ml Wristbands Material: Silicone or fabric Branding: Printed or embossed logo Promotional Merchandise Suppliers should also be able to provide other branded promotional items, including but not limited to umbrellas, key holders, USB drives, notebooks, desk accessories, gift sets, and corporate giveaways. E. Office and Corporate Materials Business Cards Size: 85 × 55 mm Printing: Full colour, double-sided Paper: 350 gsm art card Finish: Matte or gloss lamination Letterheads Size: A4 Printing: Full colour Paper: 100 gsm bond paper Compliment Slips Size: DL Printing: Full colour Paper: 120 gsm bond paper Envelopes Sizes: DL, A5 and A4 Printing: Single or full colour Paper: 100–120 gsm bond paper Note: Suppliers should demonstrate capability to print materials in: Amharic, Afan Oromo, Sidamic, Afar, Somali, Tigrinya, English and other Ethiopian languages where required. Procurement Timelines Terms of Reference Published : July 29, 2026 Deadline for Proposal Submission : August 20, 2026 Supplier Eligibility Requirements Interested suppliers must submit: Company Documentation Valid Business License Certificate of Incorporation/Registration TIN Registration Certificate VAT Registration Certificate Valid Tax Clearance Certificate Company Profile Technical Capacity Description of printing facilities List of printing equipment List of finishing equipment Production capacity per day/week Quality assurance procedures Relevant Experience Minimum three years' experience providing printing services At least three references from similar assignments Portfolio of completed work Financial Capacity Audited financial statements (last two years) or equivalent financial records Bank reference letter Proposal Submission Requirements Technical Proposal The technical proposal should include: Company Overview Company profile Years in operation Areas of specialization Relevant Experience Similar assignments undertaken NGO, donor or development sector experience Production Capacity Printing technology available Production capability Staffing structure Quality Management Quality assurance processes Sample approval procedures Reprint and defect management processes Delivery and Logistics Delivery capability Geographic coverage Turnaround times Sample Submission Suppliers should submit at least three examples of recently completed print assignments demonstrating: Colour quality Binding quality Finishing quality Branding execution Durability Financial Proposal The Financial Proposal in Ethiopian shall be submitted separately from the Technical Proposal using the Girl Effect Pricing Schedule . The Pricing Schedule has been designed to ensure a consistent and comparable evaluation of all submissions. Suppliers are requested to complete all applicable sections of the template and return it in its original Excel format. The completed pricing schedule should include, where applicable: Unit rates for all requested printing and production items. VAT and other applicable taxes. Delivery and transportation charges. Installation costs (where applicable). Minimum order quantities (where applicable). Standard production lead times. Bulk order discounts. Any additional charges or assumptions. Price validity period. Where a particular item or service is not offered, suppliers should indicate "Not Applicable (N/A)" within the template rather than deleting rows. Suppliers should not alter the structure or formulas contained within the pricing schedule unless specifically instructed by Girl Effect. The completed Financial Proposal template should be submitted together with the Technical Proposal by the submission deadline. Evaluation Criteria Relevant Experience 25% Technical Capacity 25% Quality Assurance & Samples 20% Delivery & Logistics Capability 10% Financial Competitiveness 15% References 5% Framework Management Girl Effect reserves the right to: Appoint multiple suppliers to the framework. Allocate suppliers by service category where appropriate. Conduct restricted RFQs or mini-competitions amongst prequalified suppliers. Issue direct call-off purchase orders where appropriate. Review supplier performance annually. Suspend or remove suppliers based on performance or compliance. Extend the framework period subject to satisfactory performance. Commercial and General Terms This procurement is intended to establish a non-exclusive framework agreement with multiple suppliers. Appointment to the framework does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work. Suppliers are responsible for ensuring compliance with Ethiopian tax legislation. All taxes should be clearly identified in the financial proposal. All materials developed under any subsequent call-off assignment shall become the property of Girl Effect unless otherwise agreed in writing. Successful suppliers will be required to comply with Girl Effect's safeguarding policies and may be required to undergo safeguarding checks before contract award. Girl Effect reserves the right to amend, suspend or cancel this procurement process at any stage and is not liable for any costs incurred by suppliers during the preparation or submission of proposals.

How to Apply: To apply for this opportunity, please submit a proposal by email with the subject line “**Prequalification of Printing, Branding and Production Service Providers – Ethiopia (2026–2028)** ” to **suppliers@girleffect.org** by August 20, 2026. For any questions, please also send them to our suppliers' email address.

title: Mine Action Specialist
description:
Overview of position General Background Our client supports the successful implementation of its partners’ peacebuilding, humanitarian and development projects around the world. Our mission is to serve people in need by expanding the ability of the United Nations, governments and other partners to manage projects, infrastructure and procurement in a sustainable and efficient manner. Working in some of the world’s most challenging environments, our vision is to advance sustainable implementation practices, always satisfying or surpassing our partners’ expectations. With over 7,000 personnel spread across 80 countries, our client offers its partners the logistical, technical and management knowledge they need, wherever they need it. A flexible structure and global reach mean that we can quickly respond to our partners' needs, while offering the benefits of economies of scale. Please provide general background information on the context of the engagement. Background Information - Peace and Security Cluster For over 20 years, our clients Peace and Security Cluster (PSC) has served as a key implementation platform supporting the work of its largest partner. Through a strategic partnership, PSC delivers interlinked portfolio, programme and project management services, reinforced by robust oversight and risk management controls tailored to operations in complex and high-risk environments. Operating under the leadership of the Cluster Director - who holds overall authority and accountability for PSC’s performance on behalf of its clients - the Cluster provides day-to-day management of their partners field programmes. This includes comprehensive support across human resources, procurement, contract management, planning, implementation, and financial oversight, ensuring full compliance with our client rules and regulations and donor requirements. PSC’s service delivery is complemented by cross-cutting initiatives, including knowledge and information management, gender equality, diversity and inclusion and quality assurance. The Cluster enables agile deployment and operational flexibility, allowing field programmes to respond swiftly to shifting needs in dynamic operational contexts. It also plays an essential role in donor reporting and visibility, ensuring that funding is used transparently and effectively. Background Information Established in 1997, our clients partner works to eliminate the threat of landmines, explosive remnants of war (ERW), and improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Their partner leads operational responses, coordinates mine action across the UN system, and contributes to global standards and policy development. They supports the UN's vision of "a world free of the threat of landmines and unexploded ordnance, where individuals and communities live in a safe environment conducive to development, and where mine survivors are fully integrated into their societies." Operating under mandates from both the UN General Assembly and Security Council, their functions as a specialized service within the Department of Peace Operations (DPO). They operates under UN legislative mandates of both the General Assembly and the Security Council, or at the request of the UN Secretary-General or his designated official. When instructed by the Security Council or called upon by Member States, their partner deploys under humanitarian, peace and security mandates. Their main headquarters is in the UN Secretariat, New York with a sub-office in Geneva. They provides direct support and assistance in the areas of explosive hazard threat mitigation to 18 countries/territories/missions, has a standby rapid response capacity and global technical advisors in the field of IEDs and Weapons and Ammunition Management. As an office within DPO, their partner supports peacekeeping and special political missions in accordance with Security Council mandates. They chair the Inter-Agency Coordination Group on Mine Action (IACG-MA) and leads the Mine Action Area of Responsibility under the Global Protection Cluster. It also chairs the IMAS Review Board and leads the UN Coordinating Task Force on IEDs, supporting the Secretary-General’s Disarmament Agenda. Background Information - Sudan The Sudan Programme, based in Port Sudan, works in close coordination with the National Mine Action Authority (NMAA), the UN Country Team and humanitarian partners. The project aims to protect civilians from the threat of explosive ordnance (EO) and strengthen the resilience of conflict-affected communities through a comprehensive, gender-mainstreamed and conflict-sensitive mine action response. It also supports broader humanitarian, early recovery and stabilization efforts by enabling safe access to areas contaminated by EO. Their Sudan’s key activities include land release operations, including urban EOD activities and building clearance, with the operational focus expected to shift toward the clearance of AT mines, including minimum-metal variants; delivery of both direct and indirect Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE), tailored to different gender and age groups; and provision of technical advice to humanitarian, development, and peacebuilding (HDP) actors to help them safely operate in EO-affected environments. The project also leads the coordination of the Mine Action Area of Responsibility (MA AoR) in Sudan, co-chairing the sector under the Global Protection Cluster framework. Through this role, their partner ensures that mine action is effectively integrated into humanitarian coordination mechanisms and that EO threats are adequately understood and addressed at all levels. While the Programme’s current operational footprint is primarily focused on areas under the control of the Sudan Government - especially urban areas in Khartoum and Al Jazirah - Sudan aspires to expand its outreach to all EO-affected regions, addressing both legacy contamination and new threats emerging from the ongoing conflict. Role objectives Under the direct supervision of the Head of Project Unit / Chief of Operations (HPU/CoO) or its representative, the Mine Action Specialist will perform the following tasks: Operations – Design and planning Support in providing input to the HPU or its representative on programme and project design documents from an operational and technical standpoint, such as: Workplan (e.g., nature of the threat, technical personnel and equipment requirements, etc.) Concept of Operations Input into the documents above is from the operational and technical aspects encompassing mine action pillars (e.g., clearance, explosive ordnance disposal, explosive ordnance risk education, victim assistance, advocacy, and stockpile destruction) Ensure that implementation plans have viable timelines, are assigned appropriate resources, and that implementation options reflect the knowledge of the context, as well as mechanisms and policies; key implementation documents include: Our clients Project Agreements Solicitation documents used to contract third parties (i.e., contractors and grantees) Human resources plan Support the design and planning of the national concept of operations and workplan, providing technical input to help ensure alignment with applicable standards, priorities and operational requirements. Operations - Implementation and monitoring Support and participate in the technical reviews to ensure operations are conducted in accordance with our clients policies and both International and National Mine Action standards, such as: Project management standards, Health, safety, social and environmental standards, Gender parity and mainstreaming policies, Ethics and standards of conduct, Information management systems and standards and Organizational design standards and human resources policies; Where applicable, in collaboration with the NMAC and as tasked, conduct routine on-site QA of Mine Action Organization operations (for monitoring and post-clearance inspections) and as part of the Accreditation process to ensure operations are conducted in accordance with mine action technical standards, such as: International and National Mine Action Standards (IMAS) and corresponding National Technical Specifications and Guidelines (NTSGs); Oversee, coordinate, and monitor mine action operations and performance (both operations conducted in-house and those conducted through third-party contractors and grantees). Ensure third-party contracts and grants are delivered in accordance with mine action technical, operational and quality assurance processes (Implementation Plan, SOPs, task orders issuance, accreditation). Implement the program quality management and information management system. Familiarize with and, when required, deliver EO-related courses, including SSAFE. Advise the HPU or its representative and the NMAC CoO on potential technical and operational issues that may impact the achievement of programme/project outcomes and appropriate solutions. Ensure operational plans are updated and reviewed regularly. Monitor and react to emerging trends in Land Release activities. Capacity Building & Mentorship Act as a mentor and training officer for the NMAC, providing guidance and support in operational implementation, operations management and field-level programme delivery in line with the NMAC-established priorities Develop training plans in conjunction with the HPU / CoO based on NMAC and MA Programme requirements and deliver training courses as necessary or when requested by the NMAC. Support the continuous improvement of operational practices by reviewing and updating of key documents, including Standards, Technical Guidelines, SOPs and Working practices and instructions (WPIs), in coordination with relevant stakeholders. Stakeholder management In support of the HPU or its representative, manage relationships with key stakeholders around operational and technical issues. Upon request from the HPU or its representative, engage national mine action authorities and/or relevant Government ministries for purposes of coordination. People management Mentor and advise NMAC and mine action operations personnel in planning, execution and delivery of allocated projects, ensuring incorporation of best operational processes. Promote teamwork, collaboration, and diversity by providing the Operations team with clear direction, objectives, and guidance to enable them to perform their duties responsibly, effectively, and efficiently. Foster a positive and enabling work environment, respectful of both men and women, and ensure that the highest standards of conduct are observed. Knowledge management and innovation Ensure records of operations-related files are well maintained. Effectively manage efficient and effective operations in their AOR. Keep abreast of and incorporate the latest/best practices, approaches, and technology to enhance operational results. Support e alignment of best practices and IM approaches between the NMAC. Impact of Results The MA Specialist’s effective and successful performance directly impacts the achievement of the project deliverables and mine action programme results and consequently reinforces the programme's visibility and image as well as the wider Mine Action Sector in Sudan. Project reporting Reporting on a weekly, monthly, and quarterly basis on progress to the Head of Project Unit (HPU) Ensure all reports are duly submitted and recorded in UNMAS database Key competencies An Advanced University Degree (Master’s Degree or equivalent) with a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience; or A First Level University Degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) with a minimum of 7 years of relevant experience; or A Secondary School Degree (High School of equivalent) with a minimum of 11 years of relevant experience is required. A recognised EOD Level 3 qualification is required. Preference will be given to candidates holding the IMAS Level 3+ Bulk Demolitions competency, or an equivalent nationally or organisationally recognised qualification demonstrating competence in the planning, management and conduct of bulk demolition operations. Relevant experience is defined as experience in project management in a military, humanitarian, conflict, post-conflict, or development context. A minimum of 5 years of proven and applicable experience (within the last ten years) in the conduct and management of Mine Action operations and, in particular, previous experience managing/implementing the following activities such as Explosive Ordnance Disposal, including multiple items and logistical demolitions, Non-technical survey, Technical survey, Manual mine clearance, including Road Clearance, Battle Area Clearance, Proven experience in designing and delivering training and mentorship is required (in humanitarian mine action or military or police settings), Experience in mentoring and coaching national counterparts in all core areas of mine action is required. Experience in conducting structured training and on-the-job instruction aligned with their required technical competencies is required. Training should be tailored to the needs of NMAC personnel and support their operational planning, management and field-level programme delivery. Knowledge of information management systems such as the Information Management System for Mine Action (IMSMA) is desired. Strategic Perspective - Develops and implements sustainable business strategies, thinks long term and externally in order to positively shape the organization. Anticipates and perceives the impact and implications of future decisions and activities on other parts of the organization. (For levels IICA-3 and above) Integrity and Inclusion - Treats all individuals with respect; responds sensitively to differences and encourages others to do the same. Upholds organizational and ethical norms. Maintains high standards of trustworthiness. Role model for diversity and inclusion. Leading Self and Others - Acts as a positive role model contributing to the team spirit. Collaborates and supports the development of others. For people managers only: Acts as positive leadership role model, motivates, directs and inspires others to succeed, utilizing appropriate leadership styles. Partnering - Demonstrates understanding of the impact of own role on all partners and always puts the end beneficiary first. Builds and maintains strong external relationships and is a competent partner for others (if relevant to the role). Results Orientation - Efficiently establishes an appropriate course of action for self and/or others to accomplish a goal. Actions lead to total task accomplishment through concern for quality in all areas. Sees opportunities and takes the initiative to act on them. Understands that responsible use of resources maximizes our impact on our beneficiaries. Agility - Open to change and flexible in a fast-paced environment. Effectively adapts own approach to suit changing circumstances or requirements. Reflects on experiences and modifies own behavior. Performance is consistent, even under pressure. Always pursues continuous improvements. Solutions Focused - Evaluates data and courses of action to reach logical, pragmatic decisions. Takes an unbiased, rational approach with calculated risks. Applies innovation and creativity to problem-solving. Effective Communication - Expresses ideas or facts in a clear, concise and open manner. Communication indicates a consideration for the feelings and needs of others. Actively listens and proactively shares knowledge. Handles conflict effectively, by overcoming differences of opinion and finding common ground. Fluency in English language (Reading, writing, speaking) is required Fluency in any other UN official language (Reading, writing, speaking) is desired. Team management Mentor and advise NMAC and UNMAS operations personnel in planning, execution, and delivery of allocated projects, ensuring incorporation of best operational processes. Promote teamwork, collaboration, and diversity by providing the Operations team with clear direction, objectives, and guidance to enable them to perform their duties responsibly, effectively, and efficiently. Foster a positive and enabling work environment, respectful of both men and women, and ensure that the highest standards of conduct are observed. Further information Candidates who do not hold an IMAS Level 3+ Bulk Demolitions qualification but possess an EOD Level 3 qualification must provide documented evidence of relevant operational experience in planning and conducting bulk demolitions. Such evidence may include operational logs, post-task reports, training records, or other verifiable documentation. Copies of all relevant qualifications and supporting documentation must be submitted as part of the application. EOD qualifications must have been issued by organisations that train and certify EOD personnel in accordance with IMAS Test and Evaluation Protocol (TEP) 09.30/01/2022. Applicants are responsible for providing evidence that their qualifications meet this requirement. Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.

title: Information Management Intern
description:
Organization 3iS is an international non-profit organization that provides information management services to humanitarian and development organizations. 3iS has been working in Ethiopia since 2018, supporting humanitarian partners to improve information management and analysis for decision-making. Scope of Work 3iS is seeking an Information Management (IM) Intern to support humanitarian data management, visualization, and reporting efforts. This position provides an excellent opportunity for a motivated individual to gain hands-on experience in information management, data analysis, and the design of information products. The intern will assist the IM team in creating tools, reports, and visuals to support evidence-based decision-making across projects. Main Responsibilities 1. Data Management - Assist in collecting, cleaning, and consolidating data from various sources. - Support the design and maintenance of databases, spreadsheets, and other data tools. - Ensure the quality and consistency of data for analysis and reporting. 2. Visualization and Reporting - Support the production of high-quality infographics, charts, and dashboards to visualize project data. - Assist in the creation of interactive data products and reports, ensuring clarity and alignment with 3iS branding. - Help design periodic situation reports, factsheets, and summary visuals based on project data. 3. Mapping - Assist in producing basic maps using GIS tools (e.g., QGIS or ArcGIS) for data visualization and reporting purposes. - Support the team with geographic data organization and processing. 4. Needs Assessments and Analysis - Help organize and process data for needs assessments and analysis activities. - Support the preparation of presentation materials and reports summarizing key findings. 5. Capacity Building Support - Assist in preparing training materials and content for IM training sessions. - Support virtual or in-person IM workshops as needed, including note-taking and preparation of materials. Qualifications and Experience Education Enrolled in or recently completed a degree in Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Geography, Computer Science, GIS, or related fields. Technical Skills - Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and basic data analysis tools. - Familiarity with data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau, or Canva) is a strong advantage. - Basic knowledge of GIS tools (e.g., QGIS, ArcGIS) is desirable. - Knowledge of tools like KoboToolbox, Open Data Kit (ODK), or similar platforms is an asset. - Interest in learning and applying artificial intelligence tools to enhance data analysis, reporting, and visualization workflows. Competency - Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain data quality. - Good organizational skills and ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. - Ability to work effectively as part of a team. - Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. Accountability to Beneficiaries 3iS personnel is expected to respect principles of accountability to beneficiaries of 3iS programs, in line with international standards, while actively engaging beneficiary communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of field projects. Guiding Principles Personnel is expected to respect the local culture and 3iS' policies, procedures, and values at all times. 3iS has zero-tolerance for sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, human trafficking, child abuse and exploitation. Any violations of these principles and policies will be treated as serious misconduct. 3iS is an Equal Opportunity Employer regardless of background. 3iS may carry out reference checks with other organizations on matters related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse.

How to Apply: Please apply via this link: [Information Management Intern – 3iS’s](https://3is.org/jobs/information-management-intern/) **Notes**: - Any application received by e-mail or in person will not be considered. - This vacancy will remain open for a maximum of 14 days, but it may be closed sooner if a suitable candidate is found. - This vacancy is open exclusively to candidates of Ethiopian nationality

title: Ethiopia Driver (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role Seeking a skilled, careful driver with 3+ years of experience to drive staff and materials for an international agriculture NGO. Responsibilities Regular driving and cargo management: Maintain a humble attitude of service at all times to all staff and passengers. Ensure punctuality and strict adherence to the work schedule. Follow speed limits and road rules diligently. Be adaptable to changes in vehicle routes. Develop a reliable reporting system for incidents related to the vehicle or its use. Report accidents or emergencies to your manager promptly and factually. Time, Knowledge, Office Policy, and Tool Alignment: Stay well-informed about Ethiopia road use rules and regulations. Ensure adherence to relevant safety regulations, country laws governing vehicle operations, and passenger compliance. Familiarize yourself with and adhere to the OAF’s transport and vehicle policies, as well as the driver’s pledge. File and report vehicle log books weekly, and ensure supervisor sign-off. Use the vehicle only for official purposes and report any instances of unauthorized use. Lead Vehicle Maintenance checks Regularly check and maintain vehicle equipment such as lights, windshield, horn, and brakes. Ensure that mechanical, emergency, and safety tools are in order and functional. Address vehicle maintenance needs, such as tire punctures and cleaning, as required. Conduct daily pre-departure checks on vehicle condition (fuel, oil, brakes, tires, lights). Keep the vehicle clean, inside and out, at all times. Schedule and track routine servicing and promptly report any mechanical issues. Conduct Type C vehicle Maintenance service. Logistics Support Deliver and collect documents, parcels, or goods as instructed. Support the logistics team with the loading and unloading of materials when required. Record trip details in the vehicle logbook (mileage, fuel, destination, time). Take a picture of the fuel station fuel dispenser reading, with the vehicle plate number as well as the current vehicle mileage Safety and Security Ensure that passengers wear seat belts and that safety rules are followed. Remain alert to potential security risks and follow safety procedures during all trips. Maintain a valid driver’s license and inform your supervisor of any changes or violations. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: Technical skills: Professional Driving Skills: Level 1 passenger driver’s license, proficiency in driving with a clean driving record, and ability to handle different types of vehicles. Time Management: Punctuality and the ability to adhere to a strict schedule. Communication Skills: Effective communication abilities for clear and accurate reporting. Adaptability: Flexibility to adapt to changing routes and schedules. Problem-Solving: Quick thinking and problem-solving skills, especially in emergency situations. Technical Vehicle Knowledge: Basic understanding of vehicle mechanics for routine checks and minor repairs. Cargo Management: Skills in safely managing and transporting cargo. Team Collaboration: Ability to work collaboratively with management and team members. Knowledge: Required: Fluent in Amharic and at least one Southern Nations Language (preferred: Wolayttattuwa, Hadiyyisa, or Kambaatissa Road Safety and Regulations: In-depth knowledge of local road safety laws and driving regulations. Vehicle Maintenance: Familiarity with vehicle maintenance requirements and safety checks. Organizational Policies: Understanding of organizational transport policies and adherence to them. Route Planning: Knowledge of local geography and efficient route planning. Emergency Response: Awareness of procedures for handling vehicle-related emergencies and accidents. Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Sodo, Ethiopia Benefits Health insurance, paid time off Contract Duration 1 Year Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Ethiopia. Application Deadline 20 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @ oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here ( globalhotline@oneacrefund.org ), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

title: Scholarship and Communications Coordinator
description:

title: Global Anticipatory Action Specialist
description:
About DRC   
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is an international humanitarian organization with operations in 40 countries dedicated to assisting, protecting, and finding solutions for refugees, internally displaced and other conflict-affected communities. To stay relevant and meet the needs of the people we serve, we are exploring new, innovative ways of responding to displacement crises.   
 For the past years, DRC has increasingly engaged in anticipatory action for both climate- and conflict-induced displacement. We have developed innovative tools to forecast displacement from hazards to enable humanitarian actors to get ahead of crises. In East Africa and the Great Lakes region, DRC’s AA portfolio currently encompasses five countries and expanding regional partnerships with the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and leading agencies within the AA community of practice

Overall purpose of the role: 
The Danish Refugee Council is looking for a highly experienced Global Anticipatory Action (AA) Coordinator to provide technical leadership over an assigned anticipatory action portfolio covering countries in East Africa and the Great Lakes. Who We Are

Girl Effect is an international non-profit organisation that creates media, technology and behaviour change programmes that empower adolescent girls and young people to improve their health, education and economic opportunities.

In Ethiopia, Girl Effect delivers programmes through the Yegna youth brand, reaching millions of young people through media, digital platforms, community engagement and research. These programmes require a wide range of professionally produced printing, branding and promotional materials to support programme implementation across Ethiopia

Objective

September  2026 –August 2028

title: Ethiopia Innovations and Growth Lead
description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africas farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.

To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

One Acre Fund has been working with farmers in the Amhara region of Ethiopia since 2014, with a specific focus on trees since 2018. The Ethiopia program has now expanded into the South Region of Ethiopia in 2024. Our aim with the tree program is to provide not only short-term income opportunities but also long-term benefits, such as soil health improvements and erosion control, so that farmers build resilience over time.

About the Role

The Innovations & Growth Lead will be an essential part of our leadership team in one of One Acre Funds fastest-growing country programs and report directly to the Country Director. 

As an Innovations & Growth Lead, you will sit at the intersection of high-level strategy and "last-mile" delivery, shaping the strategy to plant 100 million trees and generate over $100M additional impact for 440,000 Ethiopian farmers by 2030. You will also pioneer the revenue models that will make our impact self-sustaining.

You will lead a high-performing team of innovators and M&E specialists to turn a 5-year vision into a rigorous Learning Agenda”: designing the field trials, mastering the data, and proving what works before we scale it to 440,000 households. You will ensure that every piece of data collected in the field informs our highest-level strategic decisions. If you are obsessed with evidence-based growth and love solving complex operational puzzles in the field, this is for you!.

Success is measured by your ability to reach OAF Ethiopia’s 2030 objectives. You will:

  • Support our network of 1,000+ nursery managers by improving their production and finding new ways to generate income.
  • Engineer innovative, scalable solutions to maximize income for every farmer reached, unlocking opportunities for youth and women.
  • Secure our seed supply through large-scale adoption of the best varieties and partnerships like the Jimma Research Centre.
  • Define the next frontier and move beyond existing programs to identify "whats next." You will lead the feasibility studies to transition OAF Ethiopia from a traditional NGO model to a revenue-generating organization. In a single week, you could present our Learning Agenda to our Steerco, deciding which new programs (like carbon credits or market access) are ready for a pilot and which arent yet viable. You would then work with the Tree innovation team to turn raw avocado trial data into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for national expansion, before travelling to a remote nursery to troubleshoot a pilot in person, interviewing nursery managers to identify why avocado grafting success rates are lagging, and pivoting the training approach on the spot.

  • Translate our strategy into action: Lead multi-year impact strategies and translate them into specific field interventions across the organization.
  • Drive the "Learning Agenda": Define annual critical questions. You will decide which new services or products enter our pipeline based on scale and ROI, then set SMART objectives. For example, explore the possibility of adding high-value trees.

  • Evidence-Based Decision Making: Partner with our Monitoring & Evaluation teams to analyze trial data and drive "Go/No-Go" recommendations for the Country Director. 
  • Champion the professional evolution of your direct reports, providing the coaching and clarity needed to turn high-level organizational vision into rigorous, field-level results.

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • A proven track record with a minimum of 7 years of experience in managing complex projects or operations, or social enterprise programs in emerging markets, e.g., in agricultural innovation, extension, research & development, marketing, product development, consulting or MEL in agriculture, public health, or education (including 3+ years in one of our countries of operation).

  • Field-First Mindset: Significant experience living and working in rural or "last-mile" settings, with a deep understanding of the associated operational challenges.
  • Experimental Design & "Piloting" Mindset: Proven ability to design and execute field trials or pilot programs. You understand how to set up a "test vs. control" environment to see if a new intervention actually drives impact, you understand KPIs and success metrics and you have the judgment to adjust as needed when challenges come.
  • Evaluation Frameworks: Analyze qualitative/quantitative field data, and turn raw results into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for leadership. A plus if experience working with Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) teams to design surveys.
  • Experience managing large teams (5-10+ team members) and delivering projects successfully.

What we do
Since 1863, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has worked to preserve human dignity and relieve suffering caused by war and armed violence.In collaboration with our Red Cross and Red Crescent partners around the world, we do everything we can to deliver life-saving aid, reconnect families and locate missing people – helping those who need it most, regardless of who they are and what side of the front line they are on.We engage with authorities and armed forces on all sides, often confidentially, pressing for access to detainees to improve their living conditions and urging compliance with international humanitarian law to protect non-combatants, including from digital threats.Purpose
 
The Community Contact Center Operator is the primary point of contact between a caller and the ICRC. This front-line role is important in leaving callers with a positive impression of the ICRC and in ensuring the ICRC understands and, when appropriate, can be responsive to their needs. S/he must maintain a good overall understanding of the ICRC’s activities and operations in Ethiopia, feel a sense of ownership in responding to the queries of callers, and be able to distinguish between calls that can be addressed directly and others that will require to be routed to the appropriate departments and/or to the delegation management. S/he must also be able to understand and implement ad hoc requests from departments for specific surveys or verifications.Relationships
 



Internally, interacts with other operators and relevant counterparts in operational departments a/o support departments as well as field leaders to transmit and collect information.
Externally, interacts with people concerned with ICRC programs, receiving a/o giving information appropriately
Other ad hoc external interactions upon request



 Accountabilities & functional responsibilities
 

Responds to callers using pre-determined answers obtained from specialists in departments and filter the concerns that can be addressed immediately and those that require to be escalated;
Understands that some concerns / issues require confidential and sensitive treatment and behaves accordingly;
Immediately flags to the line manager sensitive complaints or issues involving Code of Conduct violations or requiring the involvement of the Delegation Management;
Records the details of each contact with callers in CCC (Community Contact Centre) system and ensures information received from affected people is classified into pre-determined reference categories;
Ensures all exchanges with affected people (feedback, complaints, questions and responses) are fed into the system and follow-up by relevant department specialists initiated through the line manager;
Follows-up referred complaints and feedback with the supervisor to ensure a timely response to affected people;
Compiles, cleans analyses and disaggregates data from CCC system to produce regular complaints and feedback reports;
May participate in dissemination campaigns in field locations to encourage affected people to give feedback on ICRC programs;
May be asked to participate to remote surveys (e.g. monitoring activity) or other data collection exercises (e.g. verification exercise) or to call other stakeholders (suppliers, National Society members…) and compile data accordingly;
Depending on the context, may be granted access to ICRC databases such as Prot 6, in order to perform any necessary searches and provide up-to-date information to callers.
 ADDITIONAL DUTIES
 

Acquires and maintains an understanding of the ICRC’s activities around Ethiopia by reading briefing materials, participating in regular briefing sessions, being available for field missions and by taking initiative to enquire and learn with the relevant departments.
Acquires and maintains a good understanding of the AAP framework and the ICRC’s Code of Conduct policies
Participates in the efficiency of the CCC by flagging issues and proposing improvements.
Represents the ICRC in an appropriate way during activities, in meetings and in the field, and avoids any activity that may reflect negatively on the ICRC’s image.

 Education and Professional experience required
 

First degree or Diploma in Business Administration, Social Sciences, Community Development, or relevant field
Minimum of 2 years work experience in a similar field of activity within a busy environment, preferably in the non-profit sector
Fluent in Amharic and Afan Oromo and Somali.
Preferably should also have the capability to speak other languages of ICRC intervention areas, such as Afari, Sidama, Anuak, Nuer.
Fluent in English, with ability to translate from the local languages mentioned above to English in writing.
Experience in call centre environment, with knowledge of call centre telephony and technology, is an asset
Experience in data management and practical knowledge of MS-Office (in particular Excel).
Ability to adapt to technology and IT tools.
